summary_paragraph: A male patient with type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for right upper quadrant abdominal pain and nausea with vomiting. Initial workup showed no acute findings on ultrasound or CT scan, and labs were stable aside from mild alkaline phosphatase elevation. Symptoms were attributed to a possible gastroparesis flare or mild gastroenteritis, both of which resolved with supportive care. During admission, he underwent inpatient left fifth metatarsal head resection for a diabetic foot ulcer; tissue showed Gram-positive cocci, but no antibiotics were started given lack of infection signs. Renal ultrasound revealed possible transplant renal artery stenosis and new mild hydronephrosis, though kidney function remained stable. Tacrolimus was reduced due to elevated levels, and BK virus was detected in urine requiring outpatient follow-up. He improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with a rolling walker and follow-up plans in podiatry, primary care, and transplant clinics.
